issues.description: The 3-file fence-aware duplicate_content fix (write_gate.py Gate 16, surgical_retranslate.py detector/fixer, audit_all_content.py audit check) plus the new Gate-16 regression test are implemented and verified but no commit exists.
issues.evidence: git status shows all 4 files modified, none committed; git log HEAD unchanged since befe8ec

issues.title: 2 of 4 touched files are co-mingled with large pre-existing unrelated uncommitted work
issues.description: src/translation_engine/write_gate.py (14 diff hunks, 812 lines changed total) and scripts/quality/audit_all_content.py (5 hunks, 110 lines total) each already carried substantial uncommitted modifications from other in-flight sessions/missions BEFORE this sprint's edits were made (both were already listed as modified in git status at session start, before this sprint touched them). A plain `git add <file>` would sweep unrelated work into this mission's commit, violating scope isolation.

issues.root_cause: Other sessions (consistent with the active HT-QUALITY-GATES-001 workstream visible in recent commit history) left substantial uncommitted work in these same two shared files
issues.why_not_only_symptom: A careless whole-file commit would either (a) accidentally publish unrelated, possibly-unfinished work under this mission's commit message, misattributing it, or (b) force excluding this mission's real fix along with it

issues.title: No committed regression test existed for surgical_retranslate.py's duplicate_content detector/fixer
issues.description: Prior to this audit, only src/translation_engine/write_gate.py's Gate 16 had committed pytest coverage (tests/unit/translation_engine/test_write_gate_new_gates.py). scripts/quality/surgical_retranslate.py's _detect_duplicate_content/_fix_duplicate_content had only been verified via ad-hoc, non-committed script runs during investigation -- a future edit to that file could silently regress fence-awareness with nothing to catch it.
issues.evidence: find over tests/ for *surgical* returned no matches prior to this mission
issues.root_cause: scripts/quality/ standalone repair tools have historically had partial test coverage (tests/unit/quality/ covers some scripts, not all)

issues.title: audit_all_content.py's duplicate_content check has no committed regression test (accepted limitation)
issues.description: Unlike the other two implementations, this check is inline inside scan()'s per-file loop (not a standalone function), and scan() has hard-coded CONTENT_ROOT pointing at the real D:\ content repo with no injectable root. A full end-to-end scan()-level test would require either (a) monkeypatching CONTENT_ROOT/SITES with a synthetic fixture tree exercising all upstream frontmatter/body parsing paths, or (b) refactoring the inline check into a standalone function -- both are net-new scope beyond the approved plan's 'small mechanical patch, no behavior change beyond the fence exclusion' framing, and audit_all_content.py has zero existing test coverage for any of its other 22 checks (pre-existing condition, not introduced by this mission).
issues.evidence: grep confirms no test file references audit_all_content anywhere in tests/
issues.root_cause: audit_all_content.py was written as an ad-hoc corpus-scan script, not designed for unit testing
issues.mitigation_evidence: Verified instead via literal extraction+exec of the real file's current on-disk bytes (not a hand-copy) against the real production false-positive sample plus 2 synthetic controls -- see stage1-evidence-quality-verdict.

issues.title: Other regex-based structural checks in audit_all_content.py's 23-check family were not audited for the same fence-blindness/boilerplate-collision failure mode
issues.description: The root cause fixed here (naive blank-line paragraph splitting with no code-fence awareness, on a corpus that is heavily code-example-driven SDK documentation) is a pattern, not a one-off bug. Other simple regex checks in the same file (e.g. double_period, newline_explosion) already had some fence awareness (double_period strips code via _strip pattern), but this was not systematically verified across all 23 checks in this mission -- doing so was judged out of scope for the approved plan, which targeted only the specific reported 3,622-count finding.
issues.successor_recommendation: A focused audit of the remaining checks in scripts/quality/audit_all_content.py for the same code-fence-blindness pattern, scoped as its own small mission if/when another reported metric from this audit looks suspiciously high relative to spot-checked real content.
